title: Gigs with Bud Powell
summary: He played with Bud Powell around Harlem, loved his tunes but found him unreliable with money.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Again, before Blue Note, did you ever... I think I read on a liner note for one of your recordings that you were in a session or two with Bud Powell.
It was nice. With Bud, you know... When I came to New York, Bud was going nuts, going bananas. He was hard to deal with.
Were you on an actual gig with him?
I played some gigs with him, yeah.
Oh, all around town. A place called Bowman’s up on 155th and St. Nicholas Place, and another club up in there...I can’t think of it... But I played a few gigs with him.
What did you think of his tunes?
I was crazy about them. Crazy about them. But he was bad with the money. Because he’d get the money, and by the time you got ready to get your pay, he’s gone.
